content.title: About
content.content: Greek yogurt made from nonfat milk is a thick, creamy product with high protein and low fat. It is produced by double‑straining, which removes much of the whey and creates a denser texture compared with regular yogurt.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Greek yogurt contains two to three times more protein than regular yogurt.
Nonfat milk retains most nutrients while removing almost all fat.
Traditionally, Greek yogurt is set in a temperature‑controlled environment and then strained through cheesecloth or a special filter.
Its thick consistency makes it a popular substitute for sour cream or mayonnaise in recipes.
Greek yogurt surged in popularity in the United States in the early 2000s as a high‑protein snack.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: One cup (≈200 g) provides about 20 g of high‑quality protein, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Made from nonfat milk, the product is virtually fat‑free, suitable for calorie‑restricted diets.

items.title: Source of probiotics
items.content: Live cultures promote gut health and may strengthen the immune system.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Greek yogurt supplies a substantial portion of the daily calcium requirement, important for bone health.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: The high protein and low sugar content result in a modest impact on blood glucose levels.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Although much of the lactose is removed during straining, a small amount remains.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Casein and whey proteins can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Added sugars
items.content: Some brands sweeten the product; choose an unsweetened version if you watch sugar intake.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Certain varieties may contain added salt, which should be considered on low‑sodium diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy it plain as a snack, blend into smoothies, use in sauces, dips, desserts, or as a base for dressings. Its thick texture pairs well with berries, nuts, honey, or whole‑grain cereals.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the yogurt refrigerated at 1‑4 °C. Once opened, consume within 5‑7 days and do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
